Synopsis:
After the goblins' raid on Halsin's camp, the tiefling leader berates the adventurers for causing trouble. The situation can escalate until one leader is knocked out, or it can be descalated with the aid of the player.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_RaidingParty_Confrontation.json: The lines take place just after a goblin raid on the grove/wolf‑pens: the party has returned from that fight and the camp is tense, wounded, and recovering. Zevlor, the tiefling leader, is furious—pointing to children, the dead at the gate, and accusing the adventurers of leading goblins into the den and letting a druid be taken. Aradin (and others) push back, defending the party and trading insults, so the argument quickly risks turning violent. Off‑screen, other grove figures (healers, scouts and possibly Halsin or other druids) are nearby or being tended, and the player can either step in to calm things or allow the confrontation to escalate until someone is knocked out.
- DEN_RaidingParty_PleaAtTheGate.json: Initial situation dialog. Adventurers are at the gates of the Den, pleading to be let in while tieflings refuse them entry since goblins are on their trail.
- CAMP_HalsinsRevenge_CFM.json: If the player sided with the goblins and helped sack the Grove, Halsin (if still alive) will show up at a subsequent camp night seeking vengeance. There's no way to calm him - the dialogue will always end with combat against him and some animals.
- DEN_Thieflings_RobbedAdventurer.json: Non-critpath. A human adventurer accuses a tiefling child of stealing a necklace from him. A tiefling guard may intervene if things get out of hand. 

Barth: Angry, but gruff and restrained. 
Meli: Fearless, urging Barth on.
- DEN_AdventurerLeader.json: The player is talking with Aradin in the den shortly after the goblin ambush and the player’s intervention that stopped the fight between Aradin and Zevlor. Off‑screen the grove attack has been resolved and celebrations and triage are underway; Halsin’s return or rescue and the promised tadpole discussion have been deferred until morning. Aradin is the drunk, wounded leader of a crew that was routed while hunting ruins for a relic called the Nightsong—many of his people are dead or captured, the map was lost when goblins seized his mate Brian, and he’s privately blaming himself and sulking. Other grove figures (healers, tiefling scouts or leaders, Kagha) may be nearby and the exact status of survivors or prisoners varies with prior outcomes.

context: The scene follows a tense return to the den after a goblin raid on Halsin’s camp: wounded and grieving, the grove’s people (including children and corpses at the gate) are nearby, and Zevlor the tiefling leader is furious, accusing the adventurers of leading goblins to them and allowing a druid to be taken. Aradin — a battered, drunken human leader of an adventuring crew who lost people and a map — lashes back, trading insults that quickly threaten to turn physical. Off‑screen healers, scouts and other grove figures are tending survivors, and the player can either step in to calm tensions or let the confrontation escalate until someone is knocked out.
